summary: Tested per-client branding (display name, default theme, logo stored in Object Storage) and per-user theme override, both backend and UI at 390x844. New pytest file tests/test_it12_branding.py: 17/17 pass. It covers PATCH /clients (trim, 422 for an invalid theme, 404, 403 for non-superadmin), logo upload (PNG/JPEG/WEBP accepted, resized to 256px PNG, 600x300 becomes 256x128; non-image or GIF gives 422; >1MB gives 413), logo GET (own client 200, other client 404, unauthenticated 401), DELETE logo, /branding (superadmin ?client_id; client users ignore the param), and PUT /auth/preferences (persists into /auth/me across logins, invalid value gives 422, unauthenticated 401). Regression tests test_multitenant.py and test_it11_reuse_ws.py: 17/17 pass. UI: superadmin branding follows the selected device (kowalski-a shows amber, 'Kowalski Wentylacja' and the 256px logo; chlodnia-01 shows green, fallback icon and 'Marco Polo Wentylacja'). theme-select override applies immediately and survives reload; choosing '' goes back to the client default. A Kowalski viewer sees the Kowalski logo, name and amber theme by default, no fleet card, picks light, and light persists after logout and login. Brand editor: name save, theme change, invalid file and >1MB file both show the error toast, valid upload shows the preview, remove brings back the fallback icon. Visual check of all 4 themes on Komory (manual sliders, curtain windows), Dane (charts), Ustawienia (fleet card, brand editor) and login: no horizontal overflow (scrollWidth 390). FOUND AND FIXED a bug in the green theme in index.css: 4 CSS variables pointed to themselves (--surface: var(--surface), and the same for --primary-text, --nav-bg, --thumb). That made them invalid, so in the green theme (the default) inputs, reg-cells, sensors, curtain windows, the bottom nav and the scrollbar had a transparent background. I restored the pre-theme values (#0d0d0d, #d4f0e0, rgba(14,14,14,0.86), #2a2a2a).

minor.issue: Replacing or removing a logo, or deleting a client, never deletes the old object from storage, so orphaned objects build up (soft delete is acceptable, but nothing tracks them).

ui_bugs.issue: FIXED: self-referencing CSS vars (--surface, --primary-text, --nav-bg, --thumb) made surfaces and the bottom nav transparent in the default green theme

issues: Hardcoded #c9a46a (gold) text has low contrast (about 2.3:1) on white cards: the 'RĘCZNY' mode badge (ChamberScreen.jsx:48), the heating label (ChamberScreen.jsx:35) and the alarm-mocked-banner text (AlarmRecipientsCard.jsx:49). Make it theme-aware, e.g. a var(--warn-text) that is darker (#8a6a2a) in light.
Dane chart 'Kurtyny/komin': the chimney line #c9c9c9 (DataView.jsx:103) is barely visible on white. The humidity/CO2 lines #7fa3b8/#b8a37f are also weak in light. Use per-theme chart colours.
/api/branding is called twice without client_id before devices load, so the theme briefly shows green before switching to the selected device's client theme (small flash)

rca of the issue: Green theme transparency: in index.css, the :root/[data-theme=green] block had '--surface: var(--surface)' and the same pattern for --primary-text, --nav-bg and --thumb. A custom property that references itself is invalid at computed-value time, so background: var(--surface) resolved to transparent. Mitigation: use literal values in the base theme block.
